customer_name: Hengyi Petrochemical / Shuangtu New Material (恒逸石化 / 双兔新材料)
business_problem: The fiber producer needed to replace slow, physically demanding manual inspection of spun-yarn products with a more consistent and scalable quality process, because long hours of flashlight-based visual checking were hurting quality, staffing, and energy efficiency.
solution_summary: Baidu AI Cloud helped Hengyi Petrochemical's Shuangtu New Material operation replace manual fiber inspection with an AI-driven machine-vision workflow. Along the line, industrial cameras capture multiple images from each bobbin and send them to a data center, where models analyze defects such as hair yarn, knots, oil stains, and other surface problems. The system then classifies suspicious products and feeds sorting decisions back to the production line so only true exceptions require human review. To make the models work in practice, experienced quality staff were pulled into the loop as data annotators, converting long-held defect-recognition knowledge into reusable training data. The result is not just faster visual inspection; it is a new feedback loop in which production images, labeled defect data, and continuous model tuning create a repeatable quality-control asset that can support broader manufacturing modernization across the fiber operation.

solution_components.name: Industrial Camera Array
solution_components.role: Captures high-frequency images of yarn bobbins as they move through the inspection line.

solution_components.name: Defect Classification Models
solution_components.role: Detect fiber-surface defects such as hair yarn, tangled yarn, spider-web yarn, oil stains, and knots.

solution_components.name: Industrial Intelligent Quality Inspection Solution
solution_components.role: Coordinates inspection decisions and returns routing commands to the production line.

solution_components.name: Industrial Data Intelligence Solution
solution_components.role: Turns inspection results and annotations into reusable manufacturing data for ongoing optimization.

data_flow: Twenty industrial cameras capture images of bobbins on the line, split each image into many subregions, and send them to a central analysis system. Defect-classification models judge whether a bobbin is abnormal, route suspect products for review, and use human-validated labels to improve future detection performance and production decision-making.
business_outcome: The fiber plant reduced manual inspection effort, accelerated quality checks, improved consistency, and created a data foundation that can support wider intelligent-manufacturing upgrades.
metrics: Inspection of a 20-kilogram bobbin takes 2.5 seconds.
Inspection time is reduced by more than 70%.
Twenty industrial cameras capture two bobbins at a time.
architecture_clues: Inspection now runs as a closed loop between image capture, model inference, human exception review, and additional labeling.
Experienced inspectors were converted into data annotators so their tacit knowledge could train the models.
The system is positioned as a stepping stone toward broader full-chain manufacturing intelligence.
